title: Did the Sea Swallow a Tamil City Over One Festival? | Puhar #shorts

lines.text: Did the sea swallow a city over one festival?
Puhar, at the mouth of the Kaveri, was the great harbour of the early Cholas.
lines.caps: *Puhar | at the mouth | of the *Kaveri | the great *harbour | of the early *Cholas

lines.text: Old Tamil epics describe its ships, its warehouses, and its foreign traders.
lines.caps: old Tamil *epics | describe its *ships | its *warehouses | its *foreign *traders

lines.text: Then the epic Manimekalai tells a darker story.
A grieving Chola king forgot to hold the festival of Indra, just once.
lines.caps: a *grieving | Chola *king | *forgot | the festival | of *Indra | just *once

lines.text: The goddess of the sea had warned: miss it, and Puhar drowns.
lines.caps: the *goddess | of the sea | had *warned | *miss it | and Puhar | *drowns

lines.text: The poem says the waves took the city. That is the legend.
lines.caps: the poem says | the *waves | *took | the city | that is | the *legend

lines.text: The record is quieter. Since the nineteen eighties, divers have found stone structures under the sea off Puhar.
lines.caps: the *record | is *quieter | since the *1980s | *divers | found *stone | *structures | under the *sea

lines.text: Many researchers blame slow erosion, floods and a rising sea, over centuries.
But some claim ruins out there are more than eleven thousand years old. Historians are doubtful.

lines.text: A curse, a slow sea, or a lost age? Tell me below. Then watch again, and watch the waterline.
